function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity as a natural phenomenon has been known since antiquity—ancient Greeks observed static electricity with amber (Greek *elektron*). The modern scientific study began in the 17th–18th centuries, with key figures such as William Gilbert, who first used the term *electricus*, and Benjamin Franklin, who coined the word “electricity” and performed his famous kite experiment. Subsequent discoveries by scientists like Alessandro Volta (inventing the voltaic pile), Michael Faraday (electromagnetic induction), and others laid the foundations for our modern understanding of electricity.
